learning_outcomes.text: Applies the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Applies experimental techniques to structural solids.
Determines stresses and deformations in the elastic field generated in a solid as a result of external loads.
Characterizes and analyzes structural materials using destructive and non-destructive tests. Determines stresses and deformations generated in a solid using extensometric techniques.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK 1. Characterization, analysis, and inspection of materials using destructive and non-destructive tests. Introduction to different types of characterization techniques and destructive and non-destructive tests. Presentation and interpretation of the tensile test for plastic and/or metallic materials: destructive and non-destructive.

BLOCK 2. Characterization, analysis, and inspection of materials using Extensometry techniques. Presentation of extensometric techniques: use, connections, applications. Extensometric measurements with different stress states and different configurations: tension, bending, pressure vessels....

BLOCK 3. Characterization and strength analysis using the Finite Element Method. Introduction to the Finite Element Method (FEM). Program description, general operation. Application to calculations of structural elements with different complexity in loads and restrictions.
assessment_rules: To pass the course with OPTION A, students must obtain a minimum average grade of 5 in laboratory practices, objective short-answer tests, and mixed tests (with a minimum of 4 in each mixed test if there is more than one). For OPTION B, the minimum grade for the final oral exam must be 3.5 points or higher, and students must have completed all other assessment tasks required during the course. Attendance to ALL practices is mandatory; only one unjustified absence is allowed. Failure to recover any practice within the established deadline implies a direct failure of the course. There is no second call for this course due to its eminently practical nature; it only has a single assessment call.
